findings.title: From false evidence to restorative trace
findings.claim: Joseph's shirt moves from a misleading surface to a truthful carrier of his presence. Earlier garments bear false blood or serve as evidence in a dispute; the explicitly owned shirt is sent to Jacob, where its contact brings Joseph's personal trace to his father before Yusuf himself arrives and later precedes the return of Jacob's sight. In the wider sequence, Jacob recognizes Joseph by scent while the caravan is still apart, and his sons dismiss that perception before sight returns; the shirt can be read within this sensory relay, while the text does not identify it as the scent's source. The focus word basiran also holds ocular sight alongside the separately attested inner-understanding branch: Jacob's knowledge claim in 12:96 and the supplied eye/heart contrast in 22:46 make that wider resonance legible without displacing the physical return of sight.
findings.mechanism: The focus names the garment as Joseph's and directs it onto his father's face; the explicit shirt-and-face relation brings two sides into contact before the family's arrival, while 12:9 recalls the earlier removal of Yusuf and 12:96 repeats the contact and restored sight. The earlier shirt scenes make the garment a contested witness; 12:94-96 extend recognition from scent at a distance to contact and restored sight. Jacob's statement in 12:96 that he knows what his sons do not triggers the inner-understanding branch, while 22:46 contrasts eye-sight and blindness of the heart; these meet basiran without replacing its bodily reading.
findings.reader_payoff: The shirt is newly perceptible as both evidence of the absent Yusuf's continuing presence and the material contact associated with Jacob's restored sight; the wider eye/heart contrast lets bodily seeing and inward recognition remain open together.
findings.containment: The plain reading remains a shirt placed on the father's physical face so that his eyesight returns. The recognition reading adds to that event and does not replace it. The shirt is not asserted to cause the scent in 12:94, and the packet leaves its physical healing mechanism unspecified. The 22:46 connection is a contextual parallel, not lexical proof that basiran means inwardly aware here.

epistemic.reason: The focus and supplied target text directly support the garment's prior evidentiary roles and later face-contact/sight sequence. The supplied 22:46 eye/heart contrast supports the additional inner-understanding resonance; legacy reader and HFT nominations supply the scent association, so it remains qualified rather than asserted as physical causation.

The later focus-direction connections show sight returning and the family arriving; 21:84 carries a parallel pairing of relief and family restoration.
findings.reader_payoff: The family summons reads as part of the healing's social consequence, not an unrelated logistical instruction.
findings.containment: The 21:84 comparison is a narrative analogy, not an equation of the episodes or their causes. The focus still describes literal travel and a literal return of sight.

epistemic.reason: The focus syntax, trusted cross-run finding, and supplied 12:96/99 and 21:84 texts support the relation. The Ayyub parallel is analogical, and the corroborating reader-walk source is legacy_unbound.

After the shirt is sent to restore Jacob's sight and the household is called to come, the family enters, and in 12:100 Joseph identifies the scene with the interpretation of his earlier dream in 12:4. The garment's restorative episode thus belongs to the route into the promised family scene.

The supplied 12:96 and 12:99 connections show sight returning and the family arriving; 12:100 explicitly names the final scene as the interpretation of the dream first narrated in 12:4. That sequence lets the shirt's bodily role open into the wider family culmination.
findings.reader_payoff: The command is newly perceptible as a bridge from cure to the story's long-awaited family reunion, not merely a remedy followed by a separate travel instruction.
findings.containment: The shirt is one link in the narrative chain, not the sole cause of the reunion or dream's fulfillment. The focus still gives practical commands, and 12:100 supplies the explicit dream interpretation.

epistemic.reason: The story-level sequence is explicit in the supplied focus-direction connections, but this synthesis comes from a legacy_unbound retrospective reading and remains bounded to the narrative link.

findings.title: The journey reverses direction
findings.claim: The brothers' earlier going with Joseph led to his disappearance; in 12:93 they are sent again, now carrying his shirt, and told to come back with the whole family. Jacob's fear at the first departure, his later recognition of Joseph's scent, and the family's entrance let this itinerary read as an answer to separation rather than a fresh errand.
findings.mechanism: The focus carrier idhhabu (go) returns against the departure in 12:13 and 12:15, while the paired come-to-me command and all-family wording reverse the route. The supplied 12:94 and 12:99 connections let Jacob's recognition and the family's arrival complete that reversal.
findings.reader_payoff: The brothers' movement now carries a repair: the route that once took Joseph away becomes the route that brings his father and family toward him.
findings.containment: The verbs retain their literal commands to go, cast the shirt, and bring the family. The reversal comes from their narrative relation to the supplied departure and return scenes, not from changing the verb's lexical meaning.

epistemic.reason: The legacy HFT summary lacks an exact anchor trace, but the focus word alignment and exact connection rows independently ground the separation-to-return relation; the HFT is treated only as a nomination.
